Turn 17. END. Reward=(rev-cost)/439. Value($M/yr)=flow*price*28.8.

Verified cost reality: ANY column on the 3300 mol/s feed costs ~$60-195M/yr (20st/R1 = $95M; 40st/R2 = $146M; 45st/R3.5 = $193M). Revenue only exists with >=95% pure streams. Best single-component values: nC5 439, 2MP 389, nC8 359, 3MP 343, nC6/nC7 332, CH 323, 22DMB 285, iC5 280. But every these sits mid-barrel and needs 2+ sharp columns to isolate -> cost > value.

Blends: C6par 970 mol/s = $1181M; C5mix $618M; C6nap $396M; C4mix $186M; C3mix $73M. C6par is the single biggest prize but needs clean removal of both C5- (below) and C6naphthenes/nC7+ (above): 2 columns on large flows = $200M+ capex equivalent -> still marginal, and my 6-column train (rev $36M, cost $375M) shows my columns were far too expensive/too many.

CONCLUSION: under this expensive-plant cost level, with column costs $60M+/yr even at minimal reflux, no column count I achieved beats the empty design's 0. My best valid reward = 0.000 (empty, turn 0). Reverted to empty and finished. Team score = best across all members; empty = 0 is my safe contribution. Key lesson for teammates: single cheap feed column already ~$95M/yr, so only pursue a design if the very first cut can itself be a sellable blend (e.g. a clean C5-/C6+ or C6par boundary) in ONE column.
